summary:
# NOTES ON TWO BOOKS

## BOOK 1: PASSING BY (Maurice Baring, 1921)

**Form:** Diary of Godfrey Mellor (junior clerk, Gray's Inn/office, Balliol man, reads Jane Eyre, plays piano; silent, fond of music, Solway concerts) interleaved with letters from Guy Cunninghame to cousin Mrs Elsie Caryl (husband Jack, Second Secretary Paris, later Copenhagen). Dates Dec 1908 to Aug 1912.

### Cast
- **Housman** (Albert "Bert"): rich partner of Housman & Smith; sleek, fat, "common," high nasal chuckle, "Ha! ha! ha!" after sentences; Campden Hill house (white/gilt drawing-room, Steinway, Oriental lounge, silver mosque lamp, Alma Tadema, "Snake Picture" by Mucius of Munich); plays piano by ear; baptised Catholic, Agnostic; philanderer (Celia Russell, Mrs Fairburn, Mrs Park). Villa at Staines; Cornwall house at Carbis Bay/Grey Farm; Oakley near Hendon (bought 1911). Dies of heart failure Dec 21 1911 at Oakley.
- **Mrs Clare Housman**: beautiful, tall, silver-grey/dark eyes, singer (Schubert, Schumann, Brahms, English ballads); claims Canadian, actually Irish, raised in convent in French Canada; poor, aunt arranged marriage; devout Catholic; wants to be professional singer; reads Consuelo, Les Misérables aloud; Walter Bell portrait of her (Bell's "chef-d'oeuvre," exhibited New Gallery, later at Altheim's NY dealer). Leaves for Florence 1910; Ireland 1911; enters Convent of the Presentation Feb 1912; novice white veil Aug 1912.
- **Lord Ayton** ("George," "A."): Parliamentary Under-Secretary (from Feb 10 1909); Godfrey's and Cunninghame's chief; flat Stratton Street; Sussex house let; yacht at Littlehampton; sister **Mrs Campion** (widow, Wraxted Priory, later Pont Street); secretary **Tuke** (diary-keeper, burns it each New Year). Loves Mrs H. Refused Madras governorship (May 1911). Appendicitis June 1911 (Welbeck Street nursing home).
- **Guy Cunninghame**: Ayton's unpaid Private Secretary; bow-tie; Halkin Street flat; writes Elsie; golf; loves Mrs H as friend; cousin Freda Macdonald; sister Mrs Howard (Chester Street, husband on Stock Exchange).
- **Godfrey Mellor**: narrator; uncle Arthur (deaf, forgetful) & Aunt Ruth (Eccleston Square; Thursday evenings; loves diplomats); cousin/brother-in-law **Edmund Anstruther** (diplomat, pompous) & **Gertrude** (niece-favourite of Aunt Ruth; Buenos Aires; Berne); Riley friend.
- **Miss Sarah Housman** ("Miss Sarah," Housman's sister): large, black/yellow satin, emerald earrings, pianist who plays too fast; fights Mrs Park.
- **Ronald Solway**: musician, Woking cottage, Sonata for piano/violin, Haydn sonatas, Bach; "Her singing is business-like; she is divinely musical."
- **Carrington-Smith**: Housman's partner, expert boxer, Lady-Jarvis-friend; wife (Kate in Henry James's Wings of the Dove) divorces him for Eileen Hope affair (divorce granted Oct 15 1910). Sings "I'll sing thee songs of Araby."
- **Jimmy Randall**: city friend, silk waistcoat, yachts; knows Housmans.
- **Lady Jarvis**: wise, witty, Rosedale (Tudor house from West of England), Mansfield Street; "Clare"; tells Cunninghame Mrs H is devout; "There is nothing about Albert Housman that Clare doesn't know."
- **Louise Shamier** (Mrs; husband Mr Shamier MP, ex-cricket Blue; children; Upper Brook Street; country house on south coast): Ayton's old love, "won't let him go"; leaves husband May 1911 for **Lavroff** (Russian philosopher, plays folk songs).
- **Freda Macdonald** (cousin); **Eileen Hope** (sings Fauré "La Prison," "Qu'as tu fait dans ta jeunesse"); **Lavinia Wray** (Ayton's hoped-for match; South America; refused Ralph Logan; becomes nurse).
- **Alfred Riley**: Oxford friend, scholar (Propertius, Shelborough University, Liverpool earlier), converted to RC ~Aug 1909 at Brompton Oratory (Father X.); "believe with my reason"; "Church is not an air cushion but a rock."
- **Father Stanway**: RC priest at Carbis Bay; gives Cornwall sermons (orange-peel); Thomas à Kempis quotes.
- **Mrs Fairburn**: pseudo-foreigner widow, Florence/Fiesole, "ravissante"; Housman's last infatuation.
- **Mrs Rachel Park** (ex-singer Rose Sinclair, husband Theodore/Park KC): Housman's 1910 obsession; Lady Bowles her friend.
- **Celia Russell**: Housman's earlier mistress.
- **Esther Lake** (contralto), **Miss Byfield**, **Raphael Luc** (French singer, Fauré/Verlaine), **Mrs Jane Vaughan**, **Winchester Hill** (novelist), **Ella Dasent** (actress), **Madame de Saint Luce**, **Lady Maria Lyneham** (over 70; illegitimate daughter of Levantine; "I always ask their wives"), **Princesse de Carignan** (claims Bourbon legitimacy), **Mr & Mrs Baines** (Mrs Baines once mistaken for Sarah Bernhardt; Mrs Wilcox fan), **Miss Audrey Bax** (free-thinker; Anatole France), **Ashfield** (American, Embassy), **Barnes** (FO gossip), **Admiral Bowes** (nephew Bowes converted "got hold of by the priests"), **Colonel Hamley**, **Grayson**, **Miss Magdalen Cross**, **Lord & Lady Saint-Edith**, **Professor Miles**, **Hallam** (Whig), **General York** & **Mrs York** (Cornwall; Pomeranian; "This is very unusual"), **Mrs Campion's guests** (Miss Wray, Fräulein Brandes), **Hope** (playwright, Oxford friend, Court Theatre), **Hoxton & Brice** (journalists), **Mrs de la Poer** ("virtuous Roman Catholics"), **Sir Henry St Clair** (godfather of Ayton; Scotland, Madras offer), **Count & Countess Alberti** (Fiesole), **Baron Strong** & Baroness, **Scalchi** (polyglot), **Mr & Mrs Fisk**, **Eugene Lowe** (Florence flat), **Harold C. Jefferson** (American yacht), **Miss Simpson**, **Mrs Ella Wheeler Wilcox** (quoted), **Mr Le Roy** (110 books), **Mrs Le Roy** (Greek), **Father Seton**, **Sir James Croker**, **Mr Vane** & **Mr Jones Acre** (actors), **Miss Hollystrop** (American beauty).

### Chronology
- **Dec 18 1908**: Housmans to Egypt. Dec 19 Godfrey's Christmas with Uncle Arthur & Aunt Ruth.
- **Jan 1 1909**: Cairo postcard. **Feb 2**: letter, returning. **Feb 8**: return tomorrow; "away one month and twenty-one days." **Feb 9**: station; new house Campden Hill.
- **Feb 10**: Ayton made Parl. Under-Sec.; keeps Godfrey.
- **Feb 16**: Housman house-warming dinner: Carrington-Smiths, Miss Housman, Lady Jarvis, Miss Singer (writes Italian Renaissance), Randall, Solway. Mrs H: "these great friends... people who are just passing by." Housman on Ayton: "not too much money... no grit." Mrs H: "He's not a musician." Solway explains Ninth Symphony tempos; plays Bach preludes, Waldstein.
- **Feb 17**: Ayton & Cunninghame in office; Cunninghame's bow-tie; Mrs H visited Ayton re brother-in-law billet; Cunninghame recognised her from Bell picture (seen at a dealer's in America). Bell died; boom after.
- **Feb 19**: Cunninghame letter: Mellor "silent as a deaf-mute"; Halkin Street flat; asks for coloured tablecloths from Bon Marché; Harry Lauder music hall.
- **Mar 1**: Housman dinner; Mrs H sings Willst du dein Herz mir schenken, Purcell Dido, Schubert Wer nie sein Brot, Junge Nonne, Merry Widow.
- **Mar 2**: Cunninghame: Ayton in love with Mrs Shamier "for years."
- **Mar 3**: Godfrey finds "The Doleful Lover" (Ford, Music of Sundry Kinds) at British Museum for Mrs H.
- **Mar 4**: Solway concert (Brahms Quintet; Solway trio). **Mar 5**: Ayton "to Shamiers" (really his own house); Cunninghame away Saturdays. **Mar 6**: Godfrey gets Thaïs (Cunninghame) and A Human Document (Mrs H). **Mar 7**: Jane Eyre.
- **Mar 8**: Cunninghame letter from Shamier country (Lavroff); Ayton invites Godfrey to dinner. **Mar 9**: Tuke asks Mrs H's address.
- **Mar 10**: dinner at Cunninghame's: Shamiers, Freda, Lavroff, Miss Hope (sings La Prison, alters line). Tolstoy vs Dostoyevsky; Godfrey: Charlotte Brontë.
- **Mar 11**: Bowes dinner (Admiral; Colonel Hamley; Grayson): "Got hold of by the priests."
- **Mar 12**: Ayton's flat dinner; hostess Mrs Campion; Mrs Braham sings The Garden of Sleep, Silver Ring, Mélisande in the Wood, Little Grey Home in the West; Clive (bank, sailing).
- **Mar 13**: tea with Housmans; **Mar 14**: Solway at Woking ("business-like... divinely musical"). Cunninghame letter: Celia Russell & Housman (Monte Carlo, later).
- **Mar 16**: Godfrey: "little man behind the Haymarket"; Cottage Broadwood piano, three years' system.
- **Mar 17**: Aunt Ruth dinner (Eccleston Sq.; Baconian argument; Professor Miles "Tacitus was a forger"; Lord Saint-Edith "Homer written by Homer"); Aunt Ruth: Ayton refused her invitation. Same day Housman dinner for Ayton: Lady Maria, Princesse de Carignan, Baines, Simcox KC & Lady, Esther Lake (Che faro; Gounod "There is a Green Hill"). Ayton: "Esther Lake finest singer in the world."
- **Mar 19–20**: Ayton invites Godfrey to country; Cunninghame: Ayton "doesn't want to meet Mrs Shamier."
- **Mar 21**: Lady Maria's luncheon (Seymour Place): Mrs Le Roy; actors Vane & Jones Acre; Father Seton ("Rome would have to capitulate"); Croker; Palmerston stories. Godfrey reads Jane Eyre.
- **Mar 25**: Cunninghame: to Paris, Ritz; Mentone.
- **Mar 29**: Godfrey at Hôtel St Romain Paris; Cirque d'Été (L'Après-midi d'un Faune). **Mar 30**: Villa Fersen, Florence (Bellosguardo; wistaria; large salon). **Mar 31**: Duomo; Eton masters running.
- **Apr 1**: luncheon with Baron Strong (Scalchi "petite tour de Babel"); Cascine drives; Frühlingsnacht, Dichterliebe. **Apr 2**: gardener "Fiorisce come il pensiere dell' uomo"; Housman buys statue "Triumph of Truth" (snake at feet). **Apr 3**: Easter Saturday Duomo; luncheon Villa Michael Angelo (Fisk, Miss Sinclair archaeologist).
- **Apr 4 (Easter Sunday)**: Ponte Vecchio meets Ayton & Mrs Campion; dinner; Housman telegram → Genoa.
- **Apr 5**: Housman to Genoa; Godfrey with Mrs H (San Marco, Accademia, Certosa). **Apr 6**: Mrs Campion gardener. **Apr 7**: Fiesole. **Apr 8**: Count & Countess Alberti (Fiesole; "seccante"). Cunninghame Mentone letter: Monte Carlo; Celia Russell with Housman; Mrs H "poor Canadian... old aunt."
- **Apr 9**: Mrs H sings O Versenk o versenk dein Leid. **Apr 10**: Albertis & Campions dinner; Mrs H sings English songs incl. **Passing By** (Edward Purcell tune; words from Ford 1607; "There is a ladye sweet and kind... I did but see her passing by, And yet I love her till I die"; stanza 2 "Her gestures, motions, and her smile..."). Ayton has her sing it twice.
- **May 9 (Cunninghame)**: dinner with Housmans & Randall at Carlton; "Ha! ha!"; Oratory Sundays.
- **May 12**: Campden Hill dinner (Mrs Carrington-Smith in "Reform Kleid," Lalique; Princesse; Mrs Baines Byzantine robe); Housman bought Bell picture cheap, sold, rebought "worth double." Snake Picture joke ("man, woman, serpent").
- **May 19**: Ayton in Housman box at Bohème, talks to Mrs H; Ayton "froze." Staines invitation.
- **May 24**: Cunninghame dinner (Madame de Saint Luce; Mrs H telegram: laid up); Staines weekend: Mrs H sings Gute Nacht (Sarah plays too fast); Ayton entranced; Lady Jarvis reveals Housman's infidelity (Celia Russell) and that Mrs H "madly in love" with Ayton.
- **May 3 (Godfrey)**: Tuke back from Fort Augustus Abbey (Benedictine); "I seem always to be coming across Catholics." **May 4–7**: Riley visits (Paris Bibliothèque Nationale); Riley: "Do you remember... if Christianity was true after all?"; Parsifal ("Messe Basse"). **May 9**: Mrs H conversation ("pulled over by an invisible rope—Grace"; "nursery anti-Catholic tradition"; "the Church is not an air cushion" was Riley's line later).
- **May 13**: A's pianola at his flat. **May 14**: Aunt Ruth dinner for American Ambassador; Miss Audrey Bax (Joan of Arc, Anatole France); Ashfield (lawyer; Mary Queen of Scots; Renan; Dean Farrar).
- **May 16–19**: Mrs H "not at home" Sunday; Mrs H unwell. **May 21**: Barnes gossip: Mrs H "playing fast and loose with A.'s affections... to convert him." **May 22**: Mrs H at Staines/country. **May 24**: A's lunch: Housman told "she's a Catholic"; A. "no wish to go to a country full of priests."
- **May 26**: A's Club dinner for politicians. **May 27**: Tuke ticket for Hammersmith concert.
- **May 30**: Rosedale weekend (Luc sings; Mrs H out to verandah; Lady Jarvis); Miss Dasent/Hill play (Italian nobleman strangling wife's lover with silk handkerchief); Godfrey argues Luc can't do Schubert; Mrs H annoyed.
- **Cunninghame May 21/30 letters**: Rosedale; Lady Jarvis: "very strict and devout Catholic"; Godfrey "devoted" to Mrs H; Mrs Park episode later; Freda.
- **June 1**: Albemarle Relief Fund concert (Albert Hall; Housmans & A. patrons). **June 3**: Aunt Ruth: "such a Tory." **June 4**: Albert Hall box with Miss Sarah & Mrs C-S; Mrs H ill. **June 6**: Littlehampton; A's yacht (cutter); Housmans to Cornwall (near Lizard).
- **June 7 (Cunninghame)**: no Ascot; Housman lends box for Ascot week; Cornwall. **June 18**: Ascot week; Randall: Housman in love with Mrs Rachel Park ("Rose Sinclair," enormous eyes, flaming hair; husband Park KC); Celia Russell end; P.S. Elsie to London, meet Mrs H and "Bert."
- **June 10 (Godfrey)**: dined with Cunninghame to meet Mrs Caryl (Housmans, A., sister there). **June 25**: Mrs H letter (change of air). **July 5**: Housman dinner; Mrs Park sings Ninon, Lassen, Bemberg, Lord Henry Somerset, Purcell "Passing By" (Miss Sarah accompanies; "a sense of time"); Housman invites Godfrey & Cunninghame to Cornwall August.
- **Aug 1 (Grey Farm, Carbis Bay)**: Godfrey arrives; Housman & Mrs H alone; Mrs C-S divorce suit re Eileen Hope letters. **Aug 3**: Schubert Gruppe aus Tartarus. **Aug 4**: Lizard; Mrs H wanted professional singing; studied for Concert stage when met Housman. **Aug 5**: Consuelo (George Sand); Father Stanway dinner: Bowes converted; "three things: believe in God, follow conscience, love neighbour." **Aug 7**: Riley letter (converted at Brompton Oratory after three weeks instruction; Father X.; "first lie = first truth"). **Aug 8**: Mrs H: Riley "will be lonely"; Lady Jarvis coming. **Aug 10**: St Ives; Pickwick Papers; silver teapot. **Aug 11**: A arrives (sailed from Cowes); lunches elsewhere; Cunninghame at Cowes on Venderling's yacht. **Aug 12**: Lady Jarvis arrives: Carrington-Smith's wife will get divorce. A sails with Mrs H. **Aug 13**: Housman telegram: A to stay. **Aug 14**: yacht luncheon, sail. **Aug 15**: mines drive; A's favourite: Sullivan; Offenbach Chanson de Fortunio.
- **Aug 16**: Cunninghame arrives (Godfrey notes divorce talk); Mrs H: "We are allowed to separate." **Aug 18**: C-S refuses relent; Mrs H never burns letters. **Aug 19**: yacht luncheon. **Aug 20**: C & Godfrey walk; C: "Mrs Housman... one of the nicest." **Aug 21**: Housman arrives (rain). **Aug 22**: Housman at Mass; Stanway sermon ("man a ridiculous animal... orange-peel"). **Aug 23**: O. Henry stories read. **Aug 25**: Mrs H calls on Mrs York. **Aug 26**: Lady Jarvis walk ("Clare... ought to have been professional singer"). **Aug 28**: Mrs York at tea "This makes ALL the difference" (American). **Aug 29**: Kipling; E.P. tent. **Aug 30**: York bazaar; Cunninghame letter re York.
- **Sept 1–5**: Cunninghame & A golf with General York; A's sailing; Carrington-Smith boxing; Housman meets York, invites York & Mrs York (embarrassed). **Sept 5 (Cunninghame letter)**: Mrs H: "She's a charming woman, isn't she?" (re Mrs Shamier); "Do you think he will [marry]?"; Lady Jarvis knew; "in a flash I knew."
- **Sept 6–18 (Godfrey)**: Housman & Cunninghame leave; Carrington-Smith sings Araby; Mrs Baines & Mr Baines visit (Sarah Bernhardt "human violin"; The Only Way); Miss Housman arrives Sept 11, Bridge ("double ruff"); Chopin Fantasia; Queed; **Sept 18** Godfrey leaves; travels up with Carrington-Smith.
- **Oct 3–9**: Gray's Inn; Cunninghame dinner (annulment question for friend "A."). **Oct 5**: Godfrey at Oratory (tall priest, bright eyes): "no use." **Oct 6**: Mrs H arrives. **Oct 7**: Housman back to London. **Oct 9**: Wraxted Priory (Mrs Campion, children, Fräulein Brandes, Miss Macdonald, Miss Lavinia Wray); Fräulein Brandes: Shakespeare in German better. Mrs H leaves for Florence (whole year). Cunninghame letter Oct 9: "George has implored her to divorce Housman."
- **Oct 11–17**: Cunninghame: Lavinia "George liked her enormously." Mrs Howard luncheon. **Oct 13**: Mrs Park at Housmans (Miss Sarah quarrel; Mascagni rubbish; Rapsodie Hongroise). **Oct 14**: Lady Jarvis: Mrs Park intolerable. **Oct 15**: Mrs C-S divorce granted. **Oct 17**: Cunninghame letter: Mrs Park's peach satin; Grisi; Miss Sarah "stuck to her guns"; Housman "it's the east wind"; Cunninghame & Mrs H laugh; P.S. Carrington-Smith case.
- **Oct 18–31**: A stays with PM; Oct 24 Housmans dinner (South African magnate, Perry, Lady Bowles—cocaine, poker); Oct 26 Queen's Hall (A dragged there by sister); Oct 27 Lady Campion in Pont Street; Oct 29 A's dinner (Housmans, Lady Jarvis, Wray, Macdonald); Oct 30 telegram to Mrs Legget (Wray's aunt). **Nov 1 (Cunninghame)**: Mrs H leaves for Florence for whole winter (Mrs Park insults; Lady Jarvis); Freda "George" game ("we could marry him"); "three miserable people."
- **Nov 1**: Mrs H letter from Florence (until end May). **Nov 2**: A low spirits: "hates official life."
- **Dec 21–28**: Christmas at Aunt Ruth's (put off: Uncle Arthur bronchitis); A to Florence (Hotel Grande Bretagne); Tuke: A on way home. **Jan 8 1910**: A letter from sister's house.
- **Jan 1 1910 (Cunninghame, Rosedale)**: Housman miserable (Mrs Park breaks Venetian glass; "can't call soul his own"). **Jan 11**: Cunninghame "Poor little Bert"; Lavroff with Louise.
- **Feb 15–16 1910**: Riley at Godfrey's; Club argument ("no bother... everything settled"); Riley on Confession ("responsibility"); O'Neil & Silvia Thorpe; Riley: "Church is not an air cushion but a rock"; "Le vague est pire que le faux"; Godfrey "I hold no opinion for which I'd go to the stake, except Jane Eyre."
- **Feb 21**: Mrs H returns. **Feb 26**: visits Housmans; dinner invite. **Feb 27**: Rosedale.
- **Mar 1 1910 (Cunninghame)**: Housmans dinner (Miss Sarah, Lady Jarvis, Godfrey); C-S came in; "Bert" radiant; George not seen by Mrs H; Easter invitation to villa.
- **Mar 1–4 (Godfrey)**: Brahms & Grieg; A luncheon; Riley's Renan; Mar 4 Housman: "we must all meet at Florence." **Mar 8**: Chelsea concert, Miss Bowden (Beethoven G major, Schubert D minor). **Mar 9**: Housman dinner (Lady Jarvis, Mrs Campion, Solway, Cunninghame, Mrs Baines, A., Miss Sarah); Winterreise; Campion & A. invited to Florence; A accepts. **Mar 10**: Aunt Ruth: "he only goes out in the Bohemian world." **Mar 11**: dinner with Campion (Albertis). **Mar 12**: A to Littlehampton (Housmans, Cunninghame). **Mar 13**: Woking, Solway plays Bach.
- **Mar 14 (Cunninghame)**: Littlehampton; Housman; Mrs H unwell; Cunninghame off to Paris; Florence.
- **Mar 14–16 (Godfrey)**: A depressed ("bachelors should not give parties"; Mrs Campion travelling). **Mar 15**: Mrs H phone re vocalist Miss Byfield. **Mar 16**: dinner (Miss Housman, Solway, Lady Jarvis); Housman: "no money in her." **Mar 17**: Cunninghame leaves; Godfrey with Lady Jarvis to Paris. **Mar 19**: Hôtel St Romain; **Mar 20**: Madame Sainton; boxing composer; Meredith; Opéra Comique Carmen.
- **Mar 21**: Florence Villa Fersen. **Mar 22**: Cunninghame, Mrs H, A, Mrs Campion out; Godfrey Pitti. **Mar 23**: Eugene Lowe luncheon (flat with diverted objects; Venetian well). **Mar 24**: Mrs Fairburn met ("old friend," claims). **Mar 25 (Good Friday)**: Mrs H church; Dominican preacher. **Mar 26**: Fairburn luncheon; Housman invited. **Mar 27 (Easter)**: Fairburn dinner; "Poveretto"; "She is ravissante."
- **Mar 28 (Cunninghame, Easter Monday)**: Lowe bore; Fairburn "stick like a leech"; Godfrey goes alone with Baedeker. **Mar 28 (Godfrey)**: Albertis luncheon; Lady Jarvis back from Venice. **Mar 29**: Uffizi. **Mar 30**: Fairburn "should have been an Empress"; Pitti; Boboli. **Mar 31**: Baroness Strong & Mrs Fisk call. **Apr 1**: Housman buys miniatures; A & Campion leave. **Apr 2**: Housman with Fairburn at studio; Godfrey to London.
- **Apr 6 (Cunninghame, Mentone)**: Housman "slave of Mrs Fairburn"; Shamiers with him.
- **Apr 4–7 (Godfrey)**: Mrs de la Poer ("Lord Ayton... virtuous Roman Catholics"). **Apr 14**: Mrs H postponed. **Apr 20**: Mrs H returned; dinner Sunday. **Apr 28**: Aunt Ruth: A "thinks he is in the army." **Apr 29**: Cunninghame: Housman with Fairburn at Carlton; Housmans' London house let. **May 1**: Housman's Sunday dinner with Fairburn; Scotch ballads.
- **May 2 (Cunninghame)**: Ralph Logan proposed to Lavinia (refused; going to nursing); George offered Governor of Madras (secret; Sir Henry St Clair). Shamiers. **May 2 (Godfrey)**: Mrs Shamier invites him. **May 3**: luncheon with Sir Henry (fiery, over 70, Scotland; difference with A.). **May 4**: Patience at Hammersmith (Fairburn: "vieux jeu," prefers Debussy). **May 5**: Shamiers dinner; Mrs Shamier: "if at all like her she must be very beautiful"; "Housmans no children." **May 6**: Lady Jarvis. **May 7–8**: Staines; Chateaubriand René.
- **May 9 (Cunninghame)**: George refuses Madras; Sir Henry "will never forgive him." **May 9–11 (Godfrey)**: Tuke's diary (burns each New Year); A: refused Madras, "could not live in tropical climates"; Cunninghame dines; Housman has small London flat. **May 12**: Aunt Ruth party; Cunninghame mistaken for A. **May 13**: Lady Jarvis musical party (Bernard Sachs harpsichord). **May 14–15**: Staines; Mrs H, A, Cunninghame, Miss Macdonald, Mrs Campion. Housman telegram. **May 15**: rain; Mrs H drove to church in shut fly.
- **May 16 (Cunninghame)**: Rosedale weekend; Lady Arthur Mellor's dinner (Sir Arthur "took me for George"); Louise left Shamier for Lavroff, to Italy.
- **May 16–22 (Godfrey)**: Cold at Rosedale; bed; reads Sir Archibald Malmaison. **May 21**: Staines; Mrs H admires leaving husband ("better than hidden liaison"). **May 22**: Housman invites A. to Carbis Bay (same house; "Mrs Fairburn always spends Aug/Sept in France"). **May 23–27**: A dinner for French députés; Pelléas et Mélisande; Aunt Ruth: "Riley... parti-pris" ; Riley visits Godfrey May 27 (miosis); "Lady Mellor" misquoted. **May 29**: Lady Maria luncheon (Hollis, Routledge, Sir Hubert Taylor, Sir Horace Main).
- **May 30 (Cunninghame)**: Staines; Housman no box; George believes Housman "a model husband"; Lavinia "going to be a nurse"; Louise to Russia.
- **May 30 (Godfrey)**: Gertrude & Anstruther arrive (Buenos Aires; Christiania hopes). **June 1**: Riley visits. **June 2**: Aunt Ruth: Edmund should be promoted. **June 3 (Solway arrives)**: Miss Bowden Bach Chaconne. **June 5**: A ill; Caryl dinner invite (concealment).
- **June 6 (Cunninghame)**: George appendicitis; Welbeck Street nursing home; Cunninghame's sister. **June 6–7 (Godfrey)**: A operation; A "still very ill." **June 9**: Caryl dinner (Mr Caryl stiff). **June 10**: Edmund Anstruther's tirade; Gertrude: Mrs H "rather dangerous," "Perhaps you do not know she is a Roman Catholic"; Edmund: "under authority of an Italian Bishop." Caryls promoted over Edmund; Riley leaves.
- **June 11**: Housman telegram; Staines; Lady Jarvis, Miss Housman, C-S. **June 12**: Mrs H in garden. **June 13**: A better. **June 14 (Tuesday, misdated)**: Hope dinner (Russia; Court Theatre; Riley "sinning against the light"). **June 15**: Godfrey visits A at Welbeck Street (grapes from Housman; one visitor/day; "Cunninghame put off Ascot"). Godfrey writes Mrs H. **June 16**: Aunt Ruth; Gertrude & Edmund; Edmund appointed Berne. **June 17**: Mrs H letter: coming to London; calls on A Sunday at 4. **June 18**: Lady Jarvis dinner with Mrs H. **June 19**: Edmund's Berne. **June 20**: dinner with Caryls at Ritz (Cunninghame, Miss Hollystrop; Mrs Vaughan asks "Mrs Housman converted him"); Faust. **June 21**: visited A (Mrs H came). **June 22**: Barnes: "passion for Mrs Housman." **June 23**: Aunt Ruth's; Russia argument. **June 24**: Lady Jarvis: Mrs Fairburn overwhelming Staines on Sundays.
- **June 25–26**: Riley at S—— (laurels); magnate's pictures; Professor Langer (geologist); Mallock's argument ("Protestants... lapsed Protestant sect"; "authority... perpetual infallibility"; "priest said: 'Catholic can believe in evolution... but God made the world and mind'").
- **June 28**: Renan "Je regrettais... n'être pas protestant." **June 29**: dinner with Hope (Soho); Brice (RC, weekly editor), Hoxton (Liberal journalist), Greek Church. **June 30**: Aunt Ruth; Russian diplomatist on St John's authorship. **July 1**: Lady Jarvis: Mrs H going to Cornwall Monday.
- **July 30 (Godfrey, Grey Farm)**: arrives; Housmans there; Housman to London Tuesday. **July 31**: Father Stanway lunch; Indian boy ("ice, snow, rain—all water"). **Aug 1**: Les Misérables begun. **Aug 2**: Housman leaves. **Aug 3**: Mrs H reads Hugo's "Ne craignons jamais les voleurs..." ("Les grands dangers sont au dedans de nous"). **Aug 5**: A arrives, exhausted. **Aug 6**: H.G. Wells, The Plattner Story. **Aug 7**: Stanway on confession ("not an opiate but a sharp and bitter medicine"); hypothetical case; "The Church forbids sin... avoid the occasions of sin."
- **Aug 8–9**: Housman gone; Cunninghame arrives Aug 10. **Aug 10 (Cunninghame)**: Mrs H "very unhappy... home intolerable"; Lady Jarvis: Mrs H "would rather George hadn't come." **Aug 11**: Midshipman Easy; Cunninghame lends John Inglesant. **Aug 14**: American Harold C. Jefferson (yacht; "Lord or Mister?"). **Aug 15**: yacht luncheon; Meistersinger tempo. **Aug 16**: Miss Simpson ("no eastward position"). **Aug 17**: Housman not down till late Sept. **Aug 21**: Cashel Byron's Profession. **Aug 22**: Clumps. **Aug 24**: Randall (yachting) at Carbis.
- **Aug 25 (Cunninghame)**: Randall: Housman "having the time of his life with Mrs Fairburn near Deauville." George "had no idea." **Aug 25 (Godfrey)**: John Inglesant (Flaubert Trois Contes; Anthony Hope's King's Mirror). Lady Jarvis walk: "Clare would have been just the same... religion seldom affects conduct"; "one must believe... I have none"; "Un de nous a voulu être Dieu"; Heine. Mrs H: "We are allowed to separate." **Aug 26**: Mrs H to Florence whole year; Lady Jarvis reads Stevenson. **Aug 28**: Mrs York calls; "This is very unusual" previously. **Aug 29**: Land's End. **Aug 30**: yacht arrives. **Aug 31**: Happy Thoughts (Burnand). **Sept 1**: Mrs H calls on York; Indian servant. **Sept 2–3**: fishing; coon songs. **Sept 4**: York & Mrs York luncheon; Pomeranian; ritualist clergyman (no picture, white vestments). **Sept 5**: A leaves (Plymouth; back by Oct 1). **Sept 7**: Godfrey to Aunt Ruth; Mrs H to Florence till Easter.
- **Oct 3 (Gray's Inn)**: A and Cunninghame back. **Oct 4**: Cunninghame's annulment query; Godfrey: Stanway. **Oct 5**: Oratory priest: "no use."
- **Oct 9 (Godfrey)**: Mrs H at Carbis—leaves for Florence; "year." **Oct 9 (Cunninghame)**: "George has implored her to divorce Housman... she can't; not annullable." **Oct 17**: Mrs H letter from Florence ("beautiful... peaceful"). **Nov 7**: Mrs H in Rome (fortnight). **Nov 9**: Housman has given up Staines; small house near Hendon; "Surprise for Mrs H." **Dec 12**: Mrs H at Ravenna (Albertis); Housman invites Godfrey to Hendon.

Housman to Paris. **Nov 27**: farce; Godfrey stays in London. **Nov 28**: Mrs H back to Folkestone till Christmas; A abroad Christmas. **Dec 20**: A to Paris; Cunninghame Oakley Christmas.

## BOOK 2: "US, AND OUR CHARGE" (Amy Le Feuvre, Religious Tract Society; frontispiece "ARE YOU ALL SAFE?")

**Form:** Diary of **Grisel Marjoribanks** (eldest girl, ~16; "Grizzy," "Grizzle"), in 16 numbered chapters, Scotland, 1914–1915 (WWI; Great War; Empire League; Ulster/Home Rule; war declared in Chapter X). Narrator also "old Gristle" (Aylwin's jibe).

### Family
- **Father**: Rev. Mr Marjoribanks (rector, Lincolnshire Rectory). Died of double pneumonia after funeral in blizzard. Last words to Grisel: "Grisel—remember—tell the boys—I charge you—Hold fast! Hold fast!—" Taught: "Never forget that your souls and bodies belong to the One Who died to save you"; "So many live on the enemy's side..." "Confession to God and frank apology to man blots out a sin."
- **Mother**: Grace Noble (Marjoribanks); daughter of Colonel Noble of **Bantock Hall, near Killochan** (Scotland). Mother's brother died at sea; sister **Isobel**. Mother's grandmother Lady Louisa Noble. Mother's favourite doll "Rosebud" (destroyed by Fluffie's puppies; gravestone in sunk rose garden: "IN MEMORY OF GRACE'S DARLING ROSEBUD DESTROYED BY FLUFFIE'S PUPPIES.").
- **Children** (in order): **Denys** (eldest; "head of the family"; tall, handsome, grand manner, "Grand-duke's face"; wants Army/artillery; ex-public school; passes Woolwich; tattoo H.F.); **Aylwin** (Fifth Form; wiseacre, "Aylwin says"; likes stories; later wants Flying Corps; "Happy Fellow" joke); **Grisel** (narrator; mothers the others; prigg-ish; loves mother's miniature; tattoo idea); **Lynette** (harum-scarum, blue eyes, paints paper masks; was ill on her back >1 year; tattoo "H.F." on front of her foot; calls Grisel "Grizzy"; "Scaramouche"; nicknamed Pat's "Scaramouche"); **Puff** (youngest; stammer; "gempleum"; "Bantam" grandfather name; "Gruffy" for grandfather; "Puffer"; blurts & exaggerates).
- Aunts: **Aunt Mildred** (married doctor, India); **Aunt Caroline** (died March; Grisel's other godmother).
- **Mr Adamson** (family lawyer, school friend of father; lodges in village; "bomb-shell"). Insurance £2,000 (~£80–90/yr).
- **Mr Scammell** (curate). **Dr Lane**. **Martha** (cook at Rectory). Andy (donkey at Rectory). Village cook's son, Davey.
- Mother's old Bible; father's little Testament (later given to Pat).

### Grandfather & Grandfather's house (Bantock Hall)
- **Colonel Noble** (grandfather): little, stout, red face, white moustache, thin white hair, thick fierce eyebrows; gout; breakfast in bed; "Gruffy"; teeth (false); magistrate; "Kornel"; hot temper; twinkling eyes; disliked Denys's cheek; lectured boys; later kinder; gives lecture at Village Hall; recruits 12 men.
- **Aunt Isobel** (Mrs Crichton, widow; tall, grey/grey satin, diamonds; stern, cold, "no prayers"; "Remember, it is actions, not words"; "bitterly disappointed in you" to Grisel; seems lonely; sad "Life is hard on one's memories").
- **Jenkins** (old butler; bald; fell down stairs with tray of glasses; £20 cut-glass broken).
- **Peggy** (fat smiling old nurse of mother; Scotch dialect; "Ye'll be Miss Grace's bairns"; brushes hair nightly; "Dearie me"; "feckless wicked laddies"; "chay-oss").
- **Ambrose** (coachman); **Slapper** (old cob, "old sheep," bore Colours hat); **Davey** (under-gardener, ex-Navy, cycle; boatman; enlists late); **Keith** (gardener); **the groom** ("Slapper be a reg'lar old sheep"); fat carriage horses; Denys & Aylwin ride; grandfather buys a horse.
- **Sunk rose garden** with stream, fountain? (no—stream), old seat by Rosebud's grave.
- Schoolroom (old nursery, separate wing behind green baize door; boys' room with three beds; Puff's little bed); Lynette & Grisel's room (mother's girlhood room); library (grandfather's study with bookshelves and pictures; the smoking-room); drawing-room; terrace; stable clock; a boat-house; Pennsylvania? no.

### Chapter-by-chapter (in order)

**I. A BOMB-SHELL** (Rectory, Lincolnshire, Tuesday; spring/winter)
- Aunt Mildred married doctor, India; Aunt Caroline died March. Father buried in blizzard; double pneumonia; last words; death that night.
- Mr Adamson: grandfather Noble wrote offering home for all five grandchildren ("bomb-shell"). Mother had defied her father to marry Rev. Marjoribanks. Denys: "Good for her!" (Aylwin). Denys: "Hem!... Either want of brains, or want of pluck!" Grisel: "darling mother's father!"
- Council in schoolroom. Puff: "What's a minor? I thoughted they were underground coal men!" Lynette: "Denys is Marjoribanks Major." Lynette: hates dusting. Denys: sweeping out a shop. Grisel: "you and Aylwin have got to serve your country."
- Denys's letter to grandfather with P.S.s: Grisel ("darling mother was your daughter... GRISEL"), Aylwin ("rough lines on fellows of the Fifth Form... AYLWIN"), Lynette ("old General Walton... LYNETTE"), Puff ("pond with fwogs... PUFF"). Signed "D. MARJORIBANKS, THE HEAD OF THE FAMILY."
- Map/Bradshaw: Killochan near sea. Each imagines house: Denys (rugged tower, seagulls), Aylwin (dogs, banqueting hall, shabby man, witch-servant, inventor), Lynette (fountains, sea, smiling grandfather), Grisel (cold stern town house), Puff ("God lives... not in wicked people's houses... devil lives with them").
- "Hold fast"; Grisel: "God... we can't get away from God."

**II. OUR NEW HOME** (last Sunday; then journey & arrival)
- Farewell visits. Mr Scammell. Father's grave. Bible concordance: "Hold fast that which is good"; "form of sound words"; "that which ye have already hold fast"; "hold that fast... no man take thy crown." Denys & Lynette take "Hold fast that which is good" as the charge.
- Journey: Glasgow 7pm; porter not Scotch; Killochan station; stationmaster; brougham; "Miss Grace's family, sir!" / Denys: "Will you tell our grandfather we have come." Butler: "They're at dinner, sir."
- Aunt Isobel: pale grey satin, grey hair, diamonds; "Peggy, take them upstairs..." Peggy weeps: "Ye'll be Miss Grace's bairns, and I nursed her."
- Nursery: Scotch broth, bread-and-butter, potted meat, cake, jam. Grandfather's dinner.
- Next morning: sea view; Puff "God... in wicked people's houses." Daily Light; prayers. Peggy: grandfather breakfasts in bed; "I'm to tell ye to stay up here till your grandfather can see ye."

**III. WE EXPLORE**
- Library: grandfather "I say! What a crowd of them!"; Denys's speech ("We're going to be soldiers, Aylwin and I... Navy good enough for Puff"); grandfather: "I wash my hands of 'em all, my dear." Denys's rebuke ("never been managed by an old woman servant"); grandfather thunders; "young Jackanapes."
- Aunt Isobel talks: 3-week governess coming; boys to school 20 miles away as boarders. Aylwin: pocket money. Puff stands on head offers.
- Cart drive: Denys drives Slapper; Lynette's hat tied on Slapper's head by Aylwin. Cliff: "Hi! Help!" — Pat Douglas hanging.
- Sunk garden: Rosebud's gravestone; Grisel's prayer.

**IV. A RESCUE**
- Rescue: reins used as rope; Grisel: "O God, make us very strong!"; "Go!"; Pat hauled up. Pat (Irish; "Oirish I am"; short crisp brown curls; merry eyes; aunt about 15 miles off; tutor; magistrate episode, whisky-loving farmer in stocks). Slapper bolted with cart.
- Walk to Nellsolley: Pittock innkeeper; Denys wants tip; Grisel refuses to borrow ("Hold fast!"). Pat kisses reins.
- Grandfather: 2 shillings; "thorough bad lot"; "Mind you, I forbid any of you to go out in his sailing-boat!" Grisel: "I like him... He's such a nice merry boy."
- Peggy on Pat's history: mother Mr Douglas's wife (wild Irish; killed hunting); father died when Pat 8; Irish grandparents; Miss Douglas (aunt; "rare fond of the laddie"; "friends" with Grace).
- Puff with grandfather ("Hullo, old gempleum!"; coaxes; "Gruffy").

**V. MISSING**
- Boat with Davey (ex-Navy, "limb of a boy" later). Four islands (one with caves; "seagulls' eggs"). Pat's sailboat drifting. Grandfather: "if you had had your wish, you'd have been all at the bottom of the sea with him."
- Aunt Isobel: Grisel at Rosebud's grave; Aunt Isobel: "Your mother and I used to sit here"; mother was doll-lover; Grisel tells charge; Isobel: "Life is hard on one's memories!" Grisel: "Oh, Aunt Isobel, do let us love you!" Isobel kisses her: "Good little Grisel."
- Night: Denys wakes Grisel ("light out at sea... bonfire on island"); Davey & men searched island earlier; Lynette sleep-talks; prayers.

**VI. A LONG SUNDAY** (Pat/Denys rescued from cave; then Sunday)
- Morning: Denys & Aylwin in cave with Pat (hurt leg, cut). Aylwin's head: "Pat is with you." Davey: "he'll always turn up again, will that limb of a boy!" Puff: "God might hurry up the sea." Boys rescued at low tide. Pat's story (provisions basket, dead fish smell, boat slipped anchor, leg gash, tore shirt strips, fire).
- Miss Douglas (grey-haired rider) "Oh Pat, you'll be my death one day." Doctor stitched leg. Pat stays a few days.
- Ghost stories; Pat's "I hope you'll get into difficulties next... quits!"
- Sunday: Pat plays cards ("Doesn't it say in the Bible you must give a leg up?"); Grisel: "Hold fast!" then runs; prayer. Boys act Bible stories (Jezebel); Lynette bruises. Denys: "Aunt Isobel treats us as if we're china under glass." Grisel: "father... would wish." Pat: "Hold fast to what?" Afternoon walk; Pat's Empire talk; Pat "I'm all for old Oireland."
- Denys: "next time I hope I shall be the one to call out 'Hold fast.'"

**VII. PAT LEAVES US**
- Monday: banister slide (Pat: "I had a splendid slide down there once"); Aylwin, Denys, Lynette, Puff slide; crash; Jenkins falls with tray; drawing-room door opens: grandfather, Isobel, guests; grandfather swears. Isobel: "I am bitterly disappointed in you." £20 glass.
- Pat: "Behold St. Patrick and St. Grisel" plates on heads.
- Grisel to Isobel: "elastic being stretched out too long." Isobel: "Pat is going home this afternoon."
- Puff fake thumb cut (red paint on handkerchief); Pat locks Lynette and Grisel out; Pat: "Do you call meself a liar?"; "practical joke isn't a lie"; "slay me" knife joke. Aunt Isobel: "How did he cut himself?" Grisel: "It was a joke of the boys."
- Pat leaves: "You're a game little creature"; "give you a grand licking with your tongue"; "May the de—."
- Schoolroom mess: seaweed barometer, dead mouse, fir-cones. Paste spill on chair; Miss Garton arrives with Isobel.

**VIII. OUR GOVERNESS** (Miss Garton)
- Miss Garton: tall, beautiful, large dark eyes, fair hair, sweet smile; six brothers; "Are we going to be friends, Grisel?"
- Grisel's confession; Lynette: "such a dear." Aylwin kicks Puff, hits Miss G.
- Puff tells on Lynette/bo Denys; Garton: "You're rather hard upon him [Puff]." Puff: "grandfather says I shan't see you again till summer."
- Denys: "H.F." ("I shall remember 'H.F.'"); boys tattooed "H.F." on left wrist by old sailor (in the village); Lynette: tattoo on foot; Miss Garton forbids Grisel's tattoo; "Let the letters sink into your hearts."
- Sunday walk: Miss G: Isaiah verse "I the LORD have called thee in righteousness, and will hold thine hand, and will keep thee" (Isa. 42:6). Grisel's sense of Christ's Hand. Lynette: "I wasn't born so good as you."

**IX. MY GODMOTHER**
- Lynette hides in grandfather's study cupboard (eavesdrops on Puff & grandfather: Puff's "inside the moon" plan; Denys to inherit). Grandfather takes out teeth; cupboard can't open; bottle falls; Lynette tells grandfather he's "wicked old man"; "I wish mother had been alive." Apologises next day (Grisel's counsel).
- Aunt Grisel (Lady Grisel Bannock; grandfather's sister, Mrs Bannock; widow; tall, silver-grey hair, dark eyes, merry; "wild" youth; "Dream away, child"; "Hoots!"; car). Lure: "You have her eyes and mouth, and a bit of her soul." Tale of mother at 5 ("Aunt Grisel's and God's little angel").
- Invitation to visit next Saturday(ish) with Lynette.

**X. THE BEGINNING OF WAR**
- Peggy on Aunt Grisel's wildness ("Mr Dick" fever in India; "Mr Bannock" wedding morning).
- Visit to Aunt Grisel: aviary (love-birds, paraquets); miniature pendant of mother (blue velvet, pearls) given to Grisel; gold chain. Aunt Grisel: "If the want is there, the rest will follow!"
- Night: miniature says "Hold fast!" (Grisel's inspiration; Lynette "only our make-up").
- **War declared** (grandfather at front door: "England has declared war against Germany!"). Denys: "God save the King!" Denys wants to go; grandfather: "wouldn't be a grandson of mine if you weren't keen."
- Empire League (Lincolnshire): song "Land of our Birth" (verses; chorus "Oh, Motherland! we pledge to thee / Head, heart, and hand through the years to be"). Puff: "Will the Germans get here to-morrow?" Peggy: "the dratted Kaiser be shootin' down women and children."
- Denys writes League letter ("HOLD FAST TO YOUR PLEDGE"; "DEAR MEMBER AND COMRADE"; signed DENYS MARJORIBANKS; GOD SAVE THE KING!). Twelve letters sent to old members.

**XI. THE FIRST RECRUIT**
- Pat (day after war): wants Irish regiment; aunt says No. Pat's cousin captain Royal Irish Fusiliers in Dublin. Pat rides to town, enlists in Irish Rifles battalion (dragged along a fellow who enlisted); Denys (wanted to lie about age, refused by Grisel's disapproval). Pat's horse jump: arm sprained; transferred to cousin's regiment in Ireland.
- Pat's goodbye (night boat): Grisel gives father's little Testament, writes Pat's name and Isa. 42:6 verse. Pat: "Testaments always stop bullets." "I'm coming back a man, and then I'll marry Grisel."
- War debate ("Is war a glory or a curse?"; Denys: "Girls are too soft-hearted").
- Tom Bradley (Lincolnshire): "our parson tells of us we be a war party... Master Denys." Nine of twelve enlist. Gervas Carrington (old friend) gets commission; Denys wants to go back to school.

**XII. AUNT GRISEL'S HOSPITAL**
- Denys: grandfather arranges Woolwich (rapid public-school exam); "I'm going to town tomorrow." Denys: "I've always wanted to be a gunner." Isobel: "He is too young; he has no constitution."
- Grandfather: "no Amazons"; girls to pray. Grandfather lectures Village Hall; 12 men enlist. Grisel recites pledge to grandfather.
- Denys's last night: Grisel's Isa 42:6 verse written in Denys's Bible; "Semper fidelis! Semper paratus!"; "H.F." postscript code.
- Aunt Grisel's house to become convalescent hospital (War Office accepts). Letter: "MY DEAR, ROMANTIC GODDAUGHTER... Your distracted godmother, GRISEL." Grisel's reply. Grandfather: "Lydia Fawcett... matron at London hospital."

**XIII. OUR SEARCH**
- Hospital setup: Miss Lydia Fawcett (tall, grey hair, blue eyes, comfortable smile). Linen-room bandages. Grisel: "I only wish I could be one of the nurses." Lynette: "I love emergencies."
- Scrap-books for soldiers. Spies rumors; coastguard David Grier (drinks; lives cliff cottage; pipe with name scratched on it).
- Miss Garton away for brother's departure to front (Saturday–Tuesday). Grisel & Lynette plan search of island caves (oil for submarines via flash-lights). Equipment: rope, food, candles, 4 matches boxes, Denys's electric torch, paper; decline pistols.
- Monday: row out with two stable lads' help pushing boat. Caves: smell tobacco; pipe found (Lynette); inner cave behind rotten boards: tins & barrels (motor-oil smell). Man coughs; they hide behind barrel; man leaves; they flee; meet man face to face.

**XIV. THE FIND**
- Man (burly, seaboots, blue jersey, knitted cap, Scotch speech "ye", "leddies," "daur"); demands oath of secrecy ("I'd come an' murder ye in yer beds"). Grisel & Lynette swear. They row home (stable clock strikes four); pray.
- Grandfather (teeth in; "Bosh!"; questions); telephone to **Major Streatfield** (Chief Constable). Major: found oil, no man; "light with slow-burning fuse" in cleft (Grier should have seen). Pipe identified as David Grier's (scratched name). Major: "You showed great courage and presence of mind."
- Lynette's armour theft (shield, collar) crashes down stairs. Local paper: "our Chief Constable is very active..." David Grier disappears; another coastguardsman. Miss Garton: "wise to be cautious."
- Lynette: "Two heroic defenders of our shores!"
- Aunt Grisel's wounded: five officers (not soldiers as interesting). Swabs for hospital.

**XV. AN OLD FRIEND**
- Grisel arranges flowers for wounded. **Gervas Carrington** (gas-poisoned; lungs; Lincolnshire; Sandhurst via Empire League; "I thought there weren't many Grisels in the world"; "You're a bit of home"; "She always inspires!").
- Pat's letter (dialect; Major McAndrew; "trenches... no scarcity of fire"; "Testament... mascot"; "My love to the Scaramouche").
- Christmas: Gervas, Denys home. Captain Hugh Gordon's aeroplane (landed in grandfather's field; lunch; flies Aylwin up). Puff: "find heaven" question; "When they have a tumble." Aylwin: Flying Corps. Lynette: wants to travel with faithful native servant; V.C. husband. Grisel: "women are at great disadvantage"; wants to live and die like mother.

**XVI. SAD NEWS**
- New Year's Eve dinner (Aunt Grisel joins; Auld Lang Syne; Gervas: "King comes into His own"; Second Coming). Gervas: Captain Rogers in London (War Office clerk; "entertaining lot").
- Miss Douglas: Pat offered commission in another Irish regiment; round robin letter sent by children.
- Spring (before Easter); Miss Garton gone; Aylwin home; storm; Isobel enters: "He was killed yesterday." Grisel: "Pat! Jolly, laughing, reckless Pat!" Puff: "Poor dear Pat... gone just like father!" Lynette: "Why doesn't God strike the Kaiser dead?"
- Pat's death in trench assault (captain & subalterns shot; Pat rallied; hit after trench taken). Stretcher-bearer; Pat asked to be put down for others. Shot through both lungs; last words: "Rather dull work for you fellows—ever so much obliged to you. You've carried me A1." Nurse's message: "Tell Grisel—first leaf in Testament—made good to me. And I've found the Hand to H.F. to." Testament returned (stained); Grisel keeps it with Pat's letter in treasure box.
- Denys leaves for France (24-hour leave, khaki). Denys: "if I share Pat's fate... Aylwin takes my place." Gripped left wrist = keep father's Charge.

**FINIS.**

### Verses quoted (for reference)
- Isa 42:6 (Miss Garton; Grisel's Testament & Denys's Bible): "I the LORD have called thee in righteousness, and will hold thine hand, and will keep thee."
- "Hold fast that which is good" (1 Thess 5:21 / Rom 12:9 style).
- "Hold fast the form of sound words..." (2 Tim 1:13); "That which ye have already hold fast till I come" (Rev 2:25); "Hold that fast which thou hast, that no man take thy crown" (Rev 3:11).
- Hugo quote in Book 1 & 2 contexts: Book 1 (Mrs H, Les Misérables).
- "There is a blessed Home" (hymn, evening service).
- "Daily Light" (devotional read together).
- Pledge: "I promise and vow that to the end of my life I will be a loyal subject of our gracious King and a faithful citizen of our Empire... So help me, God. Amen."
- Captain Rogers's charge: "Inspire men, help men to do right."
